chunks: Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari narrated that he said:
Ali (peace be upon him) led us in prayer at Baratha after his return from the battle against the Khawarij, and we were about one hundred thousand men.
Then a Christian descended from his monastery and asked, 'Where is the chief of this army?' We said, 'This is he.' So he approached him and greeted him.
Then he said, 'O my master, are you a prophet?' He replied, 'No, the Prophet (my master) has died.'
He said, 'Then are you the successor of a prophet?' He replied, 'Yes.'
Then he said, 'Sit, how did you ask about this?'

He said, 'This monastery was built for the sake of this place, which is Baratha, and I read in the revealed books that no one prays in this place with such a large gathering except a prophet or the successor of a prophet.'
And I have come to accept Islam, so he accepted Islam and went out with us to Kufa.
Ali (peace be upon him) asked him, 'So who prayed here?'
He said, 'Jesus, son of Mary, and his mother prayed.'
Ali (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Shall I inform you of who prayed here?'
He said, 'The Friend (Abraham), peace be upon him.'

key_terms.الْخَلِيلُ: Al-Khalil (The Friend), a title for Prophet Abraham
key_terms.بَرَاثَا: Baratha, a location where Imam Ali led prayers

ai.seo_question: Who prayed at Baratha before Imam Ali according to the Christian monk's account?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual authority of Imam Ali (AS) by linking him to the 'Baratha' location, where a Christian monk verified his status as the Prophet's successor based on scriptural prophecies regarding exclusive congregational prayer by a Prophet or his *Wasi*. The narrative underscores the continuity of divine guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt, connecting Imam Ali not only to Jesus and Mary but also to Abraham (Ibrahim al-Khalil), thereby affirming the monotheistic lineage and legitimacy of the Imams in Shia theology.
